abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sepsis is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in patients with gastrointestinal (GI) malignancies, with in-hospital mortality rates of 19.8% to 28%, significantly higher than in non-cancer patients. While sepsis outcomes have been extensively studied in the general population, large-scale population-level analyses specific to GI cancers remain limited. This study aimed to identify the outcomes of sepsis in gastric, colon, hepatic, and pancreatic cancers in the United States.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective analysis of the National Inpatient Sample (2017-2021) using ICD-10 codes, including adults ≥18 years with gastric (n=205,599), colon (n=851,120), hepatocellular (n=433,145), or pancreatic (n=557,204) cancer. Propensity matching and multivariate regression were used to adjust for confounders. A p-value of ≤0.05 was considered significant.
RESULTS: Sepsis prevalence was 13.79% in gastric, 12.6% in colon, 18.76% in hepatocellular, and 19.22% in pancreatic cancer hospitalizations. In-hospital mortality was significantly higher with sepsis across all four malignancies (gastric 23.57% vs. 5.09%; colon 17.72% vs. 2.74%; hepatocellular 22.34% vs. 6.22%; pancreatic 17.26% vs. 5.11%). After propensity matching and adjustment, sepsis was independently associated with increased mortality in gastric (aOR 1.87), colon (aOR 2.39), hepatocellular (aOR 1.60), and pancreatic cancer (aOR 1.43) (all p<0.001). Mortality among patients requiring ICU-level care was 70.28%, 70.88%, 72.97%, and 67%, respectively. Acute kidney injury, acute respiratory failure, invasive ventilation, disseminated intravascular coagulation, and shock were consistent mortality predictors across all malignancies (p<0.05). Sepsis was also associated with significantly higher hospitalization charges and longer length of stay (p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: Our study revealed that patients with gastrointestinal malignancies experience high mortality rates when affected by sepsis, with acute organ dysfunction and ICU-level care as key predictors of poor outcomes. These findings highlight GI cancer as a high-risk population for adverse sepsis outcomes and support the need for prospective studies evaluating early recognition and guideline-directed therapies.
key_points_ko: 췌장암 입원 환자 중 패혈증 발생 비율은 19.22%였으며, 사망률은 17.26%로 패혈증 미발생 환자(5.11%)보다 높았습니다.
다변량 분석 결과 패혈증은 췌장암 환자의 병원 내 사망 위험을 독립적으로 증가시켰습니다(조정 승산비[aOR] 1.43, p<0.001).
패혈증으로 중환자실(ICU) 치료를 받은 췌장암 환자의 사망률은 67%로 집계되었습니다.
급성 신손상, 급성 호흡부전, 침습적 인공호흡기 사용, 파산성 혈관내 응고(DIC), 쇼크가 주요 사망 예측 요인이었습니다.
summary_ko: 미국 전국 입원 환자 데이터(2017~2021년)를 바탕으로 위암, 대장암, 간세포암, 췌장암(pancreatic cancer) 환자에서 패혈증(sepsis)의 발생률과 사망률을 분석한 후향적 연구입니다. 췌장암 입원 환자 중 패혈증 발생 비율은 19.22%로 높게 나타났습니다. 췌장암 환자에서 패혈증이 동반되었을 때 병원 내 사망률은 17.26%로 패혈증이 없는 환자(5.11%)에 비해 현저히 증가했습니다. 특히 중환자실(ICU) 입원이 필요했던 패혈증 췌장암 환자의 사망률은 67%에 달했습니다.
title: Mortality in sepsis among patients with gastrointestinal malignancies: a nationwide analysis 2017-2021
title_ko: 소화기계 악성 종양 환자의 패혈증 사망률: 2017-2021년 전국 단위 분석
